ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (Council Regulation (EC) No 2580/2001 and CFSP decisions implementing UN Security Council resolutions), the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, and the French national asset-freezing framework under Articles L.562-1 et seq. of the Monetary and Financial Code. PEP-related enhanced due diligence is mandatory under Articles L.561-10-2 and R.561-18-1 of the French Monetary and Financial Code, covering foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs and international-organisation PEPs as defined by Directive (EU) 2018/843. The KYC file must also be screened against Tracfin typological guidance and, because the business scope involves US FDA interaction and possible USD payment rails, the OFAC SDN list is applied as a prudent internal compliance commitment; no purely French statutory obligation requires OFAC screening absent a direct US banking nexus.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), operated by INPI since 1 January 2023, with name-availability verification through the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés database on Infogreffe (www.infogreffe.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed corporate name must be expressed in Latin script; a foreign-language name is admissible provided it is transliterated into Latin characters and is not misleading as to the corporate purpose or legal form. The Loi Toubon (Law No. 94-665 of 4 August 1994) does not require a French-language corporate name, but the statutory documents filed and commercial communications made in France must be in French. The name must also respect the principle of truthfulness and must not infringe prior trademarks protected under Articles L.711-1 et seq. of the French Intellectual Property Code.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not operate a formal pre-incorporation name-reservation docket; priority is fixed by the date of RCS registration. The 30-day parameter represents the customary validity of an INPI and RCS availability-clearance certificate used internally by counsel before filing. Upon rejection of the name by the greffier of the Tribunal de commerce, the applicant may (i) request a written statement of reasons from the greffier; (ii) petition the President of the Tribunal de commerce in summary proceedings (référé) under Article L.123-5-1 of the French Commercial Code to compel registration where the refusal is unlawful or excessive; (iii) refile immediately through the Guichet Unique with a modified name after a fresh availability search; and (iv) if the rejection is grounded on a conflicting prior trademark, initiate proceedings against that mark before the competent judicial court. Administrative appeals against decisions of the INPI under Article R.411-21 of the Intellectual Property Code apply only to trademark registrations, not to RCS name registration.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only in the form of a regulated business-domiciliation arrangement under Articles L.123-11-1 and L.123-11-2 of the French Commercial Code. A third-party domiciliation contract is lawful for a SARL engaged in regulatory consulting provided the provider is authorized, maintains a physical French address, handles mail collection and offers meeting facilities. A pure virtual mailbox or an address outside France does not satisfy the siège social requirement and may trigger administrative dissolution and reclassification of French tax residence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 15% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months of operation, reflecting standard URSSAF employment-control and tax-audit patterns for low-risk consulting SARLs; the likelihood rises above 35% where the company declares no payroll, the domiciliation address hosts more than ten registered entities, or certain red flags such as cash-like transactions or inconsistent declarations are detected. Maintaining a full-time gérant, local books, and demonstrable substance documentation materially reduces the risk.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), French Ministry of Economy and Finance. Primary tax portal: www.impots.gouv.fr; business formalities and SIREN/VAT identifier registration via the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; local operational contacts are the Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) and, for non-established foreign companies, the Service des Impôts des Entreprises des Non-Résidents (SIE DRN).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a domestic French SARL: (1) file incorporation or branch registration with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce through formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, which automatically assigns the SIREN/SIRET identifiers and issues the Kbis extract; (2) the DGFiP subsequently delivers the definitive French tax identification number (TIN) and, where a taxable activity exists, the intra-Community VAT number (format FRXXSIREN); (3) the SARL must file the VAT formality on the impots.gouv.fr professional account and submit periodic VAT returns (CA3/CA12) from its first taxable operation. For a non-established foreign entity with French VAT exposure (e.g., B2B services deemed supplied in France or B2C distance sales, and services physically performed in France): apply directly for VAT registration using Form No. 15771-SD with the SIE DRN under Article 286 ter CGI; where the entity has no EU establishment, the DGFiP normally requires appointment of an accredited tax representative (Article 302 D CGI), who assumes joint and several liability for VAT and may be required to post a guarantee. No minimum-capital preface applies to obtaining tax IDs because a SARL has no statutory minimum capital requirement.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Territorial_Scope. A French SARL is by default a fully taxable French corporate resident subject to corporate income tax (Impôt sur les Sociétés, IS) on profits exploited, commercialised, or put to use in France under the territoriality rules of Articles 209 and 209 B CGI. Standard IS rate: 25% (financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2022); reduced rate of 15% applies to the first €42,500 of taxable profit where corporate turnover is below €10,000,000, the share capital is fully paid up, and at least 75% of capital is held by natural persons. The SARL is not a pass-through by default and does not benefit from a tax-exempt zone status for consulting income; profits are determined under book-tax accounting (plan comptable général) with a separate tax balance sheet.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France has no US-style check-the-box classification; however, several binding statutory elections exist: (1) option for income tax (IR) instead of IS for small SARL de famille satisfying the conditions of Article 239 bis AA CGI (close-ended capital, ≤10 partners, all family members and undisclosed and unincorporated associations of family members, not subject to IS), with the option generally irrevocable except in limited circumstances; (2) election for the reduced 15% CIT rate under Article 219 CGI for eligible SMEs; (3) election to form a fiscal group (intégration fiscale) under Article 223 A CGI where the parent holds at least 95% of capital and voting rights of qualifying 95%-or-more-owned French subsidiaries, enabling offset of profits and deficits within the group; (4) VAT elections under Article 287 CGI, including the option for cash accounting (TVA sur les encaissements), option to charge VAT on otherwise exempt financial-type services, and the OSS/IOSS regime election for cross-border distance sales and TBE digital services; (5) no elective shelter exists against hybrid mismatch rules transposed from the ATAD Directive (Articles 212 bis to 212 sexies CGI), which apply compulsorily. All elections are filed electronically through the professional tax account or with the SIE.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT / Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA) governed by Articles 256 to 289 quater of the Code Général des Impôts (CGI), harmonised with EU Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: France imposes no turnover threshold before a non-established foreign supplier must register for VAT: liability arises from the first taxable transaction (supply of services deemed taxable in France under Articles 259 and 259 A CGI, B2C distance sales of goods, and intra-Community acquisitions). For an established French business, the small-business franchise (franchise en base de TVA) under Article 293 B CGI provides a registration/taxation exemption up to €85,000 annual turnover for supplies of goods and €37,500 for supplies of services, with tolerance ceilings of €93,500 and €41,250, but the franchise is lost where the business issues VAT invoices, makes intra-Community acquisitions, supplies services not eligible for exemption, or performs cross-border activities. A resident SARL in the medical-device consulting sector is therefore registrable and must charge VAT from the first taxable euro of domestic turnover unless the franchise provision is validly claimed. For pan-EU distance sales of goods and electronically supplied services to non-taxable persons, an EU-wide mini-OSS threshold of €10,000 applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing and e-reporting reform in force under Article 289 CGI and the implementing decrees (ordonnance n° 2022-1087 and associated decrees), with a 5-corner PEPPOL-style decarbonated API model: (i) by 1 September 2026 all taxable persons established in France must be able to receive structured e-invoices via the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) or an accredited Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire (PDP); (ii) large enterprises (grandes entreprises) and mid-caps (ETI) must issue e-invoices in the crucial formats (Factur-X, UBL, or CII) and submit e-reporting from 1 September 2026; (iii) SMEs and microenterprises (PME/TPE) must issue e-invoices and transmit transaction e-reports from 1 September 2027; (iv) non-established foreign suppliers liable for French VAT must also route their invoice and transaction data through the PPF/PDP system according to the same schedule. France does not operate a real-time per-invoice digital stamping or pre-clearance system; compliance is enforced through the DGFiP's data-exchange API flows (Y1/Y2), cross-reconciliations of invoices with VAT returns, and automatic penalties for missing or non-compliant e-invoices. The mandate also expressly covers the information to be transmitted for the 'régularisation' of supplies to B2C end customers and the annual compulsory data audit trails for certified cash-register software under Article 465 bis CGI.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports: 0% VAT exemption under Article 262(I) CGI applies where goods are physically dispatched or transported by the seller, or on behalf of the seller, to a destination outside the European Union, evidenced by an accepted customs export declaration and supporting transport documents; the supplier must obtain and preserve proof of exportation within 3 months of the tax point (fait générateur) and must file the corresponding information in the recapitulative statements/intrastat declarations where applicable. Intra-EU dispatches are likewise exempt under Article 262 ter CGI (subject to a valid customer VAT ID, transport evidence, and statutory EC-sales-list reporting). Services (including FDA 510(k) and CE-mark regulatory consulting supplied by a French SARL): where the service is rendered to a taxable person established outside France, the supply is placed outside the scope of French VAT under the B2B place-of-supply rule of Article 259-1 CGI; where the customer is a non-taxable person outside the EU, the supply may be outside France if the service is effectively used or exploited outside the EU. In all service-export cases, the exporter must substantiate the customer's status and establishment through documentary evidence (foreign VAT ID or non-EU corporate registry extract, contract, engagement letter, and bank/payment records).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration / Single Administrative Document (DAU) or the electronic customs file evidencing export validation by the French or EU customs authorities

Transport evidence: Bill of Lading (B/L) or telex release for seafreight, IATA Air Waybill (AWB) for airfreight, or CMR consignment note for road transport, together with proof of goods leaving the EU territory
Intrastat / Déclaration d'Échanges de Biens (DEB) and recapitulative statement data where the destination is another EU member state
Commercial invoice, export order, and contract evidencing the offshore buyer or recipient of the goods
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT/MT103 / bank-credit evidence demonstrating that the export proceeds have been received on a French bank account within the contractual term

For services: signed engagement letter, foreign taxable-person certificate (foreign VAT number or non-EU corporate registry extract), and full fee/remuneration records proving the offshore performance or use
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France's monetary-control framework does not impose a fixed statutory FX-repatriation window for ordinary current-export proceeds; the 180-day reference is applied by the DGFiP and customs authorities as a prudential internationally accepted maximum period for evidencing export-payment collection in export-exemption audits and transfer-pricing documentation. If export zero-rating is claimed without the required documentation, or is later clawed back, the DGFiP may: (i) reassess VAT on the entire turnover within the normal 3-year limitation period of Article L.169 of the Livre des Procédures Fiscales (6 years in cases of disguised concealment of activity and 10 years where the taxpayer is not registered); (ii) apply late-payment interest of 0.20% per month under Article 1727 CGI; (iii) impose a negligence penalty of 40% of the reassessed VAT under Articles 1729 and 1730 CGI, increased to 80% for deliberate tax fraud or organized concealment under Article 1729(b) and Article 1729-0 CGI; (iv) apply automatic statutory fines for invoicing defects, including absence of mandatory invoicing information, up to 50% of the disputed invoice sums under Article 1788 A CGI; (v) reject input-VAT deductions and, in cross-border cases, engage mutual-assistance recovery under EU Directive 2010/24/EU; and (vi) refer the dossier to the competent criminal-chamber prosecutor with exposure for fraud under Articles 1741 and 1743 CGI (increased penalties for organized customs/export evasion), including imprisonment of up to five years and fines up to €500,000 for corporate officers and participating parties, plus confiscation of goods and prohibition of professional practice. The DGFiP cross-references customs exit data (NSTI / CUS), foreign-bank information-exchange agreements, and transfer-pricing documents to detect artificial, staged, or sham export structures, particularly in high-consulting-fee regulatory service invoices routed through low-tax jurisdictions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (BdF) acting within the Eurosystem; banking and financial supervision delegated to the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution); exchange control and balance-of-payments reporting oversight conducted by the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) under Articles L.151-1 to L.151-4 of the French Monetary and Financial Code.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France belongs to the euro area; the euro is fully convertible for both current and capital transactions. EU Treaty provisions on free movement of capital apply, and there is no foreign exchange control regime for movements between EU member states and third countries, except for targeted international sanctions (e.g., CFSP/European Council restrictive measures) and statistical declarations to the Banque de France. Dividends, branch profits, and capital repatriation to non-resident shareholders are unrestricted from a currency control perspective, subject only to French corporate income tax, withholding tax where applicable, and anti-money-laundering / know-your-customer documentation. Capital account transactions require monthly reporting solely for balance-of-payments statistics where the annual transaction threshold exceeds EUR 12,500,000 for resident businesses or when specifically requested.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no mandatory surrender or mandatory conversion of export proceeds into euro. French exporters may retain foreign currency proceeds in accounts opened with EU-licensed credit institutions; the only obligation is accurate invoicing, customs declaration of export transactions (via the Single Administrative Document), and inclusion in the French balance-of-payments reporting when thresholds are met. There is no statutory timeline for repatriation of export proceeds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (EUR current account) with optional designated Foreign Exchange Settlement Account
Operational Account (EUR) and separate blocked account for statutory share capital deposit (CERFA form if required)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility as supplementary payment gateway: French-licensed EMIs (e.g., Qonto, Shine, or Luxembourg/UK EMIs with EU passporting) can handle inbound/outbound wire transfers and card transactions. Legal constraints: an EMI does not provide a 'compte bancaire' in the strict legal sense (no credit institution license), so it cannot hold client funds with deposit insurance, cannot provide short-term treasury investment products, and is not suitable for the formal capital deposit requirement of a SARL. For transactional volume under EUR 1,000,000 per month and low-risk medical device regulatory consulting, an EMI is operationally acceptable but must be accompanied by a tier-1 bank account for statutory and creditor confidence.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In person appearance of the legal representative (gérant) is effectively mandatory for French tier-1 banks, especially when the beneficial owner is a non-resident shareholder. Remote opening is permitted only under an exceptional procedure of the 4AMLD/GRFP (Guide de l'Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel) if the bank offers a fully digitized 'compte professionnel en ligne' and uses a trusted third-party video-identification service; however, most compliance departments disallow remote opening for corporate entities with foreign ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs). A physical visit to a French branch is recommended for the petitioner, and for non-resident UBOs a separate video-identification plus notarised original documents can be accepted only under the internal policy of certain banks. A written mandate is insufficient; the gérant must be physically identifiable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner / gérant is a non-resident individual or legal entity from a non-EEA jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Authenticated passport or EU national ID; proof of address not older than 3 months; apostilled (Convention de La Haye) copy of the SARL's statuts; original Kbis extract no older than 3 months; French tax residence certificate of the entity; beneficial ownership declaration (Déclaration de Bénéficiaire Effectif) filed with RCS; completed bank KYC forms and PEP screening waiver; source of funds declaration showing the original capital injection from a bank in the shareholder's jurisdiction, with bank reference letter; signed engagement letter confirming no tax evasion and non-prohibited activity under EU sanctions regulations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business activity is 'Medical Device Regulatory Consulting' (ISIC 7490) – potential suspicion of indirect healthcare or public procurement exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan and service contract dossier demonstrating absence of medically regulated activities requiring a licence; professional indemnity and errors-and-omissions insurance policy; client onboarding documents (master services agreements with medical device manufacturers); ISO 9001 quality management certification if held; VAT registration certificate; evidence that the company only provides administrative/regulatory pathway advice and does not manufacture, place on the market, or act as an Authorised Representative of medical devices; chart of expected payment flow (wire/credit card invoices) showing low-risk and transparent fees.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexpected inbound cross-border wires from the parent entity or foreign investors labelled as 'capital increase' or 'loan' without prior bank notification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A notarised board resolution or shareholder decision approving the capital increase; amended statuts filed with the RCS (if share capital modification); register of shares subscribed; certificate of deposit from the notary or bank (dépôt de fonds) as appropriate; fiscal identification of the contributing shareholder; loan agreement with commercial terms, amortisation schedule, and arm's-length justification for any interest; balance-of-payments declaration to Banque de France if the contribution exceeds EUR 12,500,000 annual cumulative threshold.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or shareholder loan transfers into the SARL's French EUR account must be made via standard SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA CT for euro within EEA). The calling bank must specify the beneficiary bank (BNP/SocGen/Crédit Agricole) with the IBAN (FR76...). Compliance with French Balance of Payments reporting requires the wire to include in field 70 (remittance information) the reference 'Apport en capital – SARL' or 'Shareholder Loan – European Investment Bank Agreement', together with the unique corporate registration number (SIREN/SIRET). The French receiving bank will code the transaction under its BOP survey; for non-EEA transfers exceeding EUR 12,500 (single or cumulative), a specific BOP declaration (liaison financière avec l'étranger) may be triggered. Sanctionable practice is to avoid any split-wire or false purpose code.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For B2B trade settlements (payments to US/EU suppliers, clinical research organizations, or certification bodies), the primary clearing rail is the SWIFT network via MT103 for cross-border euro or foreign currency transfers. For documented goods or services where a performance guarantee is required, the SARL can instruct its bank to issue a commercial Letter of Credit (Documentary L/C, UCP600) or Standby L/C. Alternative rails include SEPA Instant Credit Transfers for EEA payments of less than EUR 100,000, corporate card payments (Visa Business / Mastercard Corporate) for sub-€10,000 costs, and cross-border EUR transfers via ENTERGINE, RT1 or TIPS. Each outward wire must be accompanied by a compliant purpose code (commonly 'P' for services or the applicable BOP export/import category) and complete invoice/purchase order documentation, to be retained for AML/KYC and French tax audit purposes.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD delivered forward transaction (FX Forward) under a standard ISDA or French FBF (Fédération Bancaire Française) master agreement
EUR/CHF and EUR/GBP non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies with limited convertibility in the French retail market
Cross-currency interest rate swap (IRS) where the SARL holds floating-rate offshore liabilities
Plain-vanilla currency options (calls/puts) with repo-style collateral arrangements
Spot transaction execution with split order or algorithmic execution through the bank's liquidity pool (with no change of purpose)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ordinary/Extraordinary Shareholders' Meeting (AGO/AGE) approving the statutory annual accounts and allocation of results; minutes signed and entered in the Registre des Décisions.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate organ (shareholders in general meeting); minutes held at the registered office; no government filing at this step.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of financial year-end (Art. L223-26 C.com.); calendar-year SARL: by 30 June; court-ordered extension available.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No automatic fine; any shareholder may petition the Commercial Court to appoint a court agent (mandataire de justice) to convene the meeting (Art. L223-27 C.com.); undistributed dividends remain blocked and the managing director incurs civil liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of approved annual accounts: balance sheet, income statement, notes (comptes annuels), management report and legal-publishing annexes deposited at the RCS.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via the Guichet Unique des formalités (INPI) – formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month of AGM approval and no later than 31 July for calendar-year accounts (7 months after financial year-end).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late deposit triggers a formal injunction from the Greffe and a fine of up to €1,500; after 6 months of unjustified default the Greffe applies for ex-officio strike-off (radiation) from the RCS, leading to loss of legal personality (Art. L123-5-2, R123-170 C.com.).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale): Form No. 2065-SD plus annexes 2050-SD to 2059-SD, including the managed-report schedule; filed electronically via the EFI/EDI portal.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP – Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) via impots.gouv.fr
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months of financial year-end; for calendar-year accounts: 3 May (paper) / 15 May (professional e-filers).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-payment surcharge on assessed corporate income tax (increased to 40% after 30 days) plus €150 flat penalty per omitted return and 0.20% monthly statutory interest (Art. 1728/1730 CGI).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Simplified VAT annual return (Form CA12 / No. 3517-SD) with tax reconciliation, deductible-input schedule and annual payment instalments; monthly VAT filers (Form 3310-CA3) continue their separate monthly cycle.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP via the professional télédéclaration account (impots.gouv.fr)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due simultaneously with the income tax return: 3 May (paper) / 15 May (professional e-filers) for calendar-year accounts.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-payment penalty and 0.20% monthly interest on any VAT balance due, plus €150 fixed penalty (Art. 1728 CGI); 40% increase upon concealed operations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises (CFE) – local business property levy assessed on the taxable rental value of professional premises, with a minimum contribution due even in the absence of fixed assets; CVAE is statutorily abolished as from FY2024.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP (annual assessment notice; payment online at impots.gouv.fr or by direct debit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Assessment notice issued in September/October; payment due by 15 December (online) or 20 December (other methods); balances under €150 deferred to 31 December.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-payment increase and 0.20% monthly interest, followed by compulsory enforcement measures against the SARL (saisie-attribution, legal mortgage) under Art. 1731 CGI.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Déclaration des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (DBE) – registration of ultimate beneficial owners with the RCS; annual re-certification is embedded in the Guichet Unique annual accounts deposit; any change in shareholding or control must be filed within 15 days.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: RCS (Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce) via the Guichet Unique / INPI – formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after any change in beneficial ownership, control structure or qualifying participation (≥25%); annual confirmation executed as an integral step of the annual accounts-filing transaction; no separate calendar-year UBO deadline.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal exposure: 1 year imprisonment and €15,000 fine for individuals; up to €75,000 fine for the SARL (Art. L561-1, L561-2 CMF), enforceable after formal notice from the Greffe.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax (IS) rate for FY2024; 15% reduced rate applicable to the first EUR 42,000 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs with turnover below EUR 10,000,000.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Research Tax Credit (CIR) of 30% on eligible R&D costs (up to EUR 100M base); Innovation Tax Credit (CII) of 20% on eligible innovation expenses up to EUR 400,000; JEI status granting total or partial IS exemption; 10% preferential rate on net patent licensing / embedded IP income (IP Box).
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward, but annual utilization capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable income exceeding EUR 1,000,000; carryback available up to EUR 1,000,000 for 5 years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065 ('Déclaration de résultats') with annexes 2050 to 2065-SD, filed electronically via the EFI/EDI service on impots.gouv.fr (TéléTVA); CVAE no longer due since FY2024.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with four quarterly IS advance instalments (acomptes).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months of the fiscal year-end; 31 December year-ends: filing due 3 May of the following year; final balance due 15 May; instalments due 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, 15 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SIREN, APE/NAF code, legal form, registered office, tax group reference, and régime d'imposition selection.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident SARL: enter French registered-office address and PE identification; declare through the Non-Resident Fiscal Department (SFNR) if no permanent establishment in France.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting result before tax adjustments (per audited financial statements under French GAAP).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident: attribute to the French PE only income economically connected to French activities, in line with Art. 209 CGI and the OECD Authorized Approach.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sch. 2058-A Aggregation: reintegration of non-deductible expenses (excess amortization, unsupported provisions, fines, non-deductible car leases) and deduction of items such as patent amortization.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reinstate head-office charges recharged to the French PE only if invoiced at arm's length and supported by substance documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax loss carryforward claimed for the year and utilization of prior losses under the capped formula.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PE: claim losses only against French-source profit; losses of the foreign head office are not imputable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of corporate income tax: apply 15% reduced rate to the first EUR 42,000 of taxable profit and 25% to the remainder.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify eligibility for the 15% rate: paid-up capital fully subscribed and paid, turnover below EUR 10M, and at least 75% of shares held by individuals. Non-resident corporate shareholders may disqualify the SME rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 3.3% social contribution on the portion of taxable profit exceeding EUR 763,000, where turnover exceeds EUR 7,630,000.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PE: apply the 3.3% contribution on French PE profits above the threshold unless covered by an exemption instruction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reporting of CIR, CII, and other tax credits against IS.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credits are available only to the French taxpayer; offset is limited to the IS liability computed on French-source profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of four quarterly instalments and the final balance due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: One-off payments via TéléTVA; non-resident entities without a French bank account must use the SFNR wire-transfer procedure and provide bank identifiers by 15 January of the filing year.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or missing filing triggers a 10% automatic surcharge plus 0.20% per month late interest (Art. 1727 CGI); 40% for bad faith and 80% for fraudulent maneuvers (Art. 1729 CGI); unpaid taxes trigger a 5% cash penalty (Art. 1731); repeated violations expose the company to enforcement liens and publication of the tax debt.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% statutory withholding tax on dividends paid to non-resident corporate shareholders (Art. 119 bis 2 CGI); 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the parent holds >= 5% for 24 months; non-resident individuals: 12.8% PFU plus 17.2% social levies (30% combined) subject to treaty and social-security coordination.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Invoke treaty relief by submitting Form 5000/5001 tax-residence certificate endorsed by the foreign tax authority, accompanied by Form 2561 ('demande d'exonération/restitution de retenue à la source'); the forms must reach the DGFiP (or the paying French entity) before the distribution or within the statutory claim period; the beneficiary must evidence economic substance and intended-beneficiary status to survive the MLI Principal Purpose Test.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to non-residents for rights used in France: 33.33% statutory WHT (Art. 182 B CGI); DTA rates typically 0% for software copyright and 5-15% for patents/know-how; the EU Interest & Royalties Directive may exempt related-party qualifying payments. Interest (arm's length) to non-resident lenders: 0% WHT, except 75% on sums paid to persons in non-cooperative jurisdictions (Art. 238 A CGI).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000,000 annual pre-tax turnover (Local File/Master File); EUR 150,000 share capital and >50% foreign shareholding triggers the documentation duty irrespective of revenue; Country-by-Country report required where the group's consolidated revenue >= EUR 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not apply a Gulf-style ESR regime, but the GAAR (abus de droit, LPF Art. L.64), the MLI Principal Purpose Test, and substance-over-form case law deny treaty benefits and deductibility to artificial arrangements. A MedTech regulatory consultancy must demonstrate real French substance: qualified sign-off staff, contracts actually performed in France, premises, and decision-making for FDA 510(k)/CE-Mark submissions, rather than pass-through fee invoicing to offshore affiliates.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of taxable profit, concealed activity (activité occulte), fictitious invoicing for FDA/CE regulatory services, or diversion of revenues to a tax-haven parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to EUR 500,000 and 5 years' imprisonment for individuals; legal persons fined up to EUR 2,500,000 (Art. 131-38 CP); tax reassessment at 80% penalty rate for bad faith plus 0.20% monthly interest (Art. 1729 CGI).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors prosecuted as principals or accomplices (Art. 1741 CGI); personal civil solidarity for unpaid taxes, bank-account freezes, travel bans, and disqualification from company management for up to 15 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to submit Form 2065 and annexes before the statutory deadline, late payment of instalments, or non-registration of the French SARL with the RCS.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 10% automatic surcharge plus 0.20% monthly interest; 40% penalty for bad faith; 80% for fraudulent maneuvers; ex-officio assessment (taxation d'office) and withholding of VAT refunds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The managing director (gérant) becomes personally liable for the persistence of the filing default; personal fine up to EUR 1,500 and potential in solidum liability where the failure results from gross mismanagement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Abuse of Law (Abus de droit)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SARL held to be artificial or interposed solely to channel MedTech consulting fees to a low-tax jurisdiction while lacking real staff, premises, or operational activity in France.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization under LPF Art. L.64 with a 80% penalty on reassessed sums; refusal of treaty exemptions under the PPT; forfeiture of the 15% SME rate and CIR/CII credits; reclassification of distributions as non-deductible.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors liable in solido for the reassessed tax under Art. 1807 CGI; judicial freezing of personal assets, travel restrictions, and disqualification from managing French companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issue or receipt of forged invoices for FDA 510(k)/CE-Mark 'certification' services never performed, cash-driven operations, or laundering of proceeds through the SARL.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: False-invoicing offense: up to EUR 500,000 fine and 5 years' imprisonment (CGI Art. 1743; CP Art. 313-2); money laundering: up to 10 years' imprisonment and EUR 750,000 fine for legal persons (CP Art. 324-1); 80% fiscal penalty plus asset seizure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers exposed to personal restitution, travel bans, account-freezing orders, and imprisonment; civil liability toward creditors under the corporate-veil piercing doctrine (action en comblement de passif).
